finding.text: The task folder has no `task.jsonl` (only session.jsonl, review.jsonl, past-work.md), though requirements.md says to log progress and answer review findings there. A fresh agent cannot tell what landed, what the review answers were, or what is next.

Only piece (a) + queue + turn-taking is in the diff. Echo suppression, highlight dropout, (c) karaoke/phrase streaming and (b) tap-to-pause are all absent, and nothing in the folder records them as open or deferred. Echo matters most: `BargeIn.speaking()` and the new auto-resume trust the mic level, which the read-aloud voice itself raises, so the voice can hold or restart its own reply.

A question is detected only by a trailing "?" (`BargeIn.js` `heard_speech`, `/\?\s*$/`). requirements.md also says "or a reply to it is coming". A spoken question that Whisper punctuates with a full stop is resumed over the incoming answer, and the bar shows no drop.

The "resume control on the bar" is only a changed tooltip on `$play` (`ReciteBar.js`, `this.$play.attr("title", …)`). The diff has no visible resume button, and no shot shows the `heard` or `paused` bar. Either add a distinct control or write down that Play is the resume control, with a shot.

After a question drops the reply (`BargeIn.js` `heard_speech`), `state` is set to "off" and the timer cleared, but `sync()` is not called. Since `try_resume` does call it, check that the mic and the listening state come back for the next interruption. The test sets `barge.on = false`, so it cannot catch this.

`wait_at`, `quiet_since_wait`, `wait_timer`, `turn_wait_ms` (Recite.js) and `resume_timer` (BargeIn.js) are used but not declared as fields. `turn_wait_ms` is read through `?? 1500`. The readme's state/field list should name them, and `readme.md` Use should mention `quiet_ms` and `turn_wait_ms` as settings.

The tests drive `heard_speech` and `pause` directly, so the real route (the mic-level check, then Whisper text, or the wire line via `owner_spoke`) is untested. The shots (`shots/piece-a-demo-page.png`, `piece-a-tests-pass.png`) show only the demo page and the test pass, not the phone-width sheet that requirements.md asks for.

`read()` is now the only path that calls `stop()` before queuing. The doc says so, but check `Sheet.js` `read_aloud()` for a session switch. A different session's replies now queue behind the old session's, which may not be wanted. `READ_ALOUD_V` was not bumped because `Sheet.js` is untouched.
The architecture doc admits `chunks` never shrinks until `stop()` (memory over a long session). This is acknowledged and acceptable, but it should be filed as an open item in the readme or handover.

`BargeIn.speaking()` (BargeIn.js, new, ~line 27 of the patch) reads `this.level`, but `level` is only updated in `hear()` while a mic is open and `close()` never resets it. After a barge-in closes the mic (`heard_speech(..., {close_mic:true})`, BargeIn.js:125) the last loud level stays, so the next queued reply sees `speaking()` true and `check_wait()` polls forever without playing. Make `speaking()` false when `!this.mic`, or reset `level` in `close()`, and add a test for it.

A second owner line while already `heard` is ignored: `owner_spoke()` returns early unless state is playing/loading, so "wait… / what about the other one?" does not drop the old reply; it resumes after 1.5 s and then talks over the new answer. The question rule in requirements 1(a) should also apply when `recite.state === "heard"` (call `heard_speech` again to cancel or reschedule).

The task folder has no `task.jsonl`, but requirements.md says progress and review answers go there as `{"review":{"answer":...}}` lines. Only `review.jsonl`, `session.jsonl`, `inbox.jsonl` and `past-work.md` exist, and none shows the 13 review findings answered or the merge landing. A fresh agent cannot tell what is answered, merged or next. Add the task.jsonl lines.

"No flood" from the 21:01 section is neither built nor recorded as deferred. Queued replies release after `turn_wait_ms = 1500`, not the 2–3 s window asked for. There is no "most relevant reply first" ordering and no collapse of agent updates into "I have an update on X". The readme's "Open, by the agreed build order" list (readme.md) omits it, so the next agent will not pick it up. Add it as an open item, or build the window change if it is small.

The "Open, by the agreed build order" list names echo, highlight dropout, tap-to-pause, resumable bubbles and karaoke, but leaves out the later asks: the bubble toolbar and voice chevron, replay with `replay_audio`, the raised mic threshold while playing, and lit words. The list also links `read-aloud-next/requirements.md` under a date-dated session path. Complete the list so a fresh agent has the whole queue.

The readme "Watch out" still says "words that match the sentence being read are ignored" and that echo cancelling removes most leakage. The echo merge has not landed (the owner heard the voice leak into the mic), so those statements are untrue today. Mark them as not built yet, or move them to the open list.

The docs (architecture.md, comments in BargeIn.js, Recite.js, Recite.css) cite "review finding 3/5", "error 4" and "review note 8". They point at a review that a reader of the code cannot open and will read as noise once the folder moves. Plain descriptions of why would age better.

`shots/` holds only `piece-a-bar-400/1200`, demo-page and test-pass images. The requirements call for 400x860 and 1200 shots of the sheet half open while a long reply is read. That is only partly relevant to piece (a), since the highlight and scroll are in (c), but the queue merge asked for a proof that no playback starts until quiet, which the unit test covers and no shot shows.

Played ids are marked at queue time (Recite.js `final()`), so a reply cut off by a reload before it is spoken is never read, which contradicts "never skips an unplayed one". The architecture doc records the choice and its reason; the compromise is acceptable until resumable bubbles land.

Recite.js `queue()` (the `if (this.state === "idle") this.start_or_hold(first)` line) skips held replies: while a reply is held for the owner's speech the state is still `idle`, so a second reply (or the next streamed sentence from `take()`) calls `start_or_hold` again with its own later `first` index, overwriting `wait_at`, and the earlier held chunks are never spoken. The "no double or skipped phrase" ask is broken; `queue()` should leave `wait_at` alone when it is already set, and the "waits for quiet" test should queue two replies while talking and assert both play in order.

Item 20 ("never skips an unplayed one") is not met: `final()` calls `Recite.mark_played(id)` when the reply is queued, so a reply that is then dropped (by `drop_heard()`, a question, or a session switch) or lost to a reload before it was read is recorded as played and never read. Mark it when its last chunk finishes, or unmark it on `stop()`; architecture.md acknowledges the queue-time choice but the requirements ask for the other behaviour.

readme.md "Watch out" still says "Echo cancelling removes most of it, and words that match the sentence being read are ignored", but no echo code exists yet (no `echoCancellation`, no text matching in `audio/Recite/` or Dictate), and the same page's new "Open" section lists echo as not built. Reword the line to say it is planned, so a fresh agent is not misled.

`drop_heard()` in `final()` drops the paused reply and everything queued behind it whenever any fresh reply arrives while `state === "heard"`, including a second reply or an agent update unrelated to the owner's line. Requirements say a new reply queues and only a new question drops the rest; the diff reads "a reply is coming" as "this reply answers the question". Narrow it to the reply that follows the owner's line, or record this as the chosen alternative in the requirements' "Resolve, don't park" form.

The test for "resume from the cut sentence's start" calls `r.play(1, 1.5)` and checks `audio.currentTime === 0` against a stubbed audio object, so it proves `resume(true)` calls `play(at, 0)` but not that the real element restarts. A shot or a real-audio check would be firmer; none was asked for this piece, and `shots/` is absent, which is fine for (a).

BargeIn.js `try_resume()` after the check path (`close_mic: true`) resumes 1.5 s after the line arrives with the mic closed, so quiet is assumed rather than measured; the owner speaking again right after the line would be talked over. Acceptable until echo work, but worth a line in architecture.md.
ReciteBar.js:~425 chains `.attr(...).tc(...)` on `$play`; this assumes `attr` returns the view. Not verified here; the demo page at /framework/audio/Recite/ would show it quickly.

No `task.jsonl` answer lines or merge record were checked from this review's folder alone; a fresh agent can continue from requirements.md plus the readme "Open" section, whose order matches "Order now", but the 21:01 "no flood" asks (2–3 s quiet window, prioritise the direct answer, one collapsed update line) are neither built nor listed in that section. Add them there.

A new reply arriving while the old one is paused by barge-in calls `drop_heard()` -> `stop()`, which empties `chunks` and so also throws away every reply already queued behind it (Recite.js `drop_heard`, `final`, `partial`). requirements.md ("Turn-taking") says the owner speaking mid-reply keeps "the rest queued" and only a new question drops it. Drop only the interrupted reply's remaining chunks (keep later queued replies), or write the alternative beside the decision.

The "never starts while I speak" proof stubs `barge.speaking = () => talking` (Recite.test.mjs, "proof item 14"). The owner's ask was mic speech, then a reply, then no playback until quiet; add one test that drives the real `BargeIn.level`/`hear()` path so the threshold logic in `speaking()` is covered.

Docs carry build history instead of the structure. doc/architecture.md bullets cite "review finding 3/5", "review note 8/9", "an earlier version marked it...", and Recite.css and BargeIn.js comments say "(finding 4)", "(finding 5)". CLAUDE.md law 9 says "verified against the code, no history"; state what the code does and drop the review numbers.

The readme's "Open, by the agreed build order" list is missing items the requirements added later: the thinking cue (`thinking_cue`), `read_aloud_hidden`, the async-update one-liner, `replay_audio`, and the raised mic threshold while playing (item 22). A fresh agent working only from this list would not know them; link requirements.md sections or add them. Also state that the no-flood quiet window is still 1.5 s (`turn_wait_ms`), not the 2-3 s the owner asked for, so it is clear that piece is not done.

The task folder has no task.jsonl and no outcome line. Only session.jsonl, review.jsonl and an unlabelled `shots/` exist, and the last session line says the merge is still pending. requirements.md asks for progress and review answers in task.jsonl; add the outcome and next-piece lines so the folder stands alone. Index `shots/` (piece-a-bar-400.png, piece-a-bar-1200.png and the rest) in that record. The 400 and 1200 shots show only the bar, not the sheet half open during a long read, which was only needed from piece (c) on.

`heard_speech()` on a question calls `recite.stop()` but leaves `this.live` set. If the old reply was still streaming, the later `take()` queues only the unsent tail, so a half reply is read. Consider `this.live = null` in `stop()` or `drop_heard`.

`check_wait()` polls every 80 ms with `setTimeout` (Recite.js ~L182). CLAUDE.md says "stream, don't poll", but this is a local mic-level timer, not network data; it is acceptable. Say so in architecture.md, since the doc already describes the poll.

`speaking()` and the fast check share the threshold, but `speaking()` requires `barge.on`. With the ear off, a reply never waits for the owner, which seems intended; mention it in the readme settings paragraph.

audio/Recite/doc/architecture.md (the new bullets, diff lines 653-661) narrates history ("used to empty chunks", "now still gets", "could stick true forever", "no longer skips"). CLAUDE.md law 9 says a system's doc states what is true now, no history; reword each bullet as the current rule and its reason.

ext/drawer/readme.md:34 (the Read-aloud paragraph) is stale: `Sheet.read_aloud()` now calls `recite.stop()` when it switches to a different session (Sheet.js:71), and the readme never says so. Add one sentence there, not only in Recite's architecture.md.

audio/Recite/readme.md "Open, by the agreed build order" (diff lines 694-709) is a roadmap pasted into a module readme and repeats requirements.md. It will be wrong after the next merge. Link the task's requirements instead, or keep one line per open item, and keep the readme to present state.

The task folder cannot be continued from alone. The requirements.md holds eight dated amendments with no "landed / next" summary, and the progress log is `session.jsonl` (the earlier review's "no task.jsonl" finding was answered with an append.mjs redirect, which a fresh agent will not know). Add a short status block at the top of requirements.md or a `status.md`: piece (a) landed in bac868a77; echo, highlight, tap, bubbles, karaoke are not started.

The work covers only piece (a), the queue and turn-taking, and the played flag. Echo, no-flood, the thinking cue, highlight dropout, tap-to-pause, replay and karaoke follow are all open. That matches the owner's stated order, but the "Prove it" shots (400x860 and 1200, sheet half open, highlight moving) are not due until the later pieces. `shots/` holds only bar and test-run images (piece-a-bar-400.png, piece-a-bar-1200.png).

Requirements for (a) say quiet is "about 1.5 s", but the later "No flood" amendment wants one 2–3 s window. Recite.js (`turn_wait_ms`) and BargeIn.js (`quiet_ms`) are two separate 1500 ms constants for the same idea, and the bar `Recite.js` `check_wait` repeats a fallback (`?? 1500`) for a field that always has a value. When no-flood lands, make this one setting.

Recite.js `check_wait` polls every 80 ms with `setTimeout`. It reads a local mic level, so "stream, don't poll" does not apply, as architecture.md says. It could simply be driven from `BargeIn.hear()` frames (they already fire), which would remove `wait_timer` and `quiet_since_wait`.

`Recite.queue()` is not behind a hold when the ear (barge) is off, so with the ear off a reply starts over the owner. This is documented in readme "Watch out", but note that "never start while I speak" has no mic level to go on in that mode, so it is only as good as the chat's own mic.
Recite.js (drop_heard comment) dates a change "2026-11-02" while the other comments say 2026-11-01. Use one date convention.

The near-silent drop only covers the own-mic path: it lives in `trigger()` (BargeIn.js, diff line ~192, `this.peak < this.near_silent`), but `owner_spoke()` (the chat-line path, the normal one on the phone, and where the owner's "Thank you." phantom came from) only gets the blocklist and the fuzzy echo match. The requirement says "drop Whisper finals on near-silent audio" and `barge.level` is already known there; either gate `owner_spoke` on the recent level too, or say in architecture.md why it can't.

The new tests cover only the echo match and two phantoms (Recite.test.mjs, the two added tests). Nothing exercises `near_silent`, `echo_threshold_mult`/`effective_threshold()`, `echo_guard_ms` expiry (an echo line arriving after 1.5 s is not dropped), or the required "unrelated owner line is sent". Add one test per guard; the requirement asked for proof by test.

"Recent read text" is not matched: `echo()` compares against the chunk being read (architecture.md says "the chunk being read"), but the requirement says "the sentence being read or the recent read text", and `echo_guard_ms` exists precisely because the leak lands after the sentence ends. Once playback moves to the next chunk, the tail of the previous one (still arriving through Whisper's lag) no longer matches. Keep the last one or two read chunks for `echo()`.

The `echo_active()` window starts when "playing" ends, so a barge-in pause (`set("heard")`) sets it too, and the owner's own real reply right after is judged against it. It is harmless for unrelated words, but the 1.6x raised threshold then applies to the owner's genuine speech just after a barge-in, delaying `schedule_resume()` pushes. Say so in architecture.md or limit the guard to the end of a chunk, not a pause.

`MicStream.constraint()` now forces `echoCancellation` and `noiseSuppression` for every mic opened through MicStream (MicStream.js:70), including Dictate and push-to-talk, not just Recite's barge-in mic. MicStream/readme.md is not in the diff and does not say so; add one line there (and a way to turn it off) so a dictation agent isn't surprised by changed audio.
Comment dates: the new comments say "2026-11-02" while the task folder, requirements and earlier code say 2026-11-01. Use one convention.
`static noise()` is a plain regex list; the phantom list will grow. A small array constant would be easier to extend than editing the regex.
The shots (`shots/piece-echo-tests-pass.png`) show test output only, not the bar or demo page. Fine for a logic-only piece.

The echo, near-silent and phantom guards in `BargeIn.owner_spoke()` (BargeIn.js:88-90) only stop the barge-in; the owner asked that these lines be dropped and "never sent", but the diff does not touch the Dictate send path (`ux/Dictate/`), so "Thank you." and echoed text still land in the chat as phantom lines (requirements.md, Echo bullets 1-3). Either gate the send in Dictate (agree with mastermind-ink-check, who owns that file) or write in readme.md/architecture.md that only barge-in is guarded and record the send-side gap as an open item.

This task folder cannot be continued alone: there is no `task.jsonl` here (the brief says progress and review answers go there), only `session.jsonl`, `review.jsonl` and `inbox.jsonl`. Add the `{"review":{"answer":...}}` lines for the earlier review findings and a landing line for the echo and thinking-cue pieces, or say in the report where they live.

The thinking cue fires on every non-assistant `chat.text` in `from_wire` (Recite.js, `schedule_cue()` call after the `owner_spoke` line). That includes lines typed by the owner or by agents, and it plays even when `barge.on` is false and nobody is speaking. The brief says the cue plays "soon after the owner stops speaking", while a reply is pending. Restrict it to the owner's own lines, or say in architecture.md that it fires on wire arrival and why that is close enough.

`recent_peak` decays by 0.995 per ~8 ms frame and keeps decaying during `transcribing` (BargeIn.js `hear()`). After a long Whisper transcription a real but quiet line could fall under `near_silent` (0.045) and be dropped as a phantom, so it would not pause the reply. Worth a phone test, or hold the peak while transcribing.

`BargeIn.noise()` still treats any text that starts with `(`, `[`, `*` or `♪` and ends with the matching mark as noise. Fine for Whisper marks, but a real line such as "(wait) hold on *" is also dropped. Low risk.

The mic threshold factor (`echo_threshold_mult`, item 22) and the `echo_active()` guard are documented in readme.md and architecture.md. The known trade-off, that the guard also starts after an ordinary barge-in pause, is recorded in architecture.md. No gap there.

The tests cover echo dropped / unrelated line barges in, phantom, near-silent, and the cue (once, again at 2 s, stops on reply, skipped while playing, off switch), as the brief asked. There are no phone-width shots for these pieces. That is fine, since the brief only asks for shots on the karaoke pieces. The shot files in `shots/` are test-pass screenshots.

Making `MicStream.constraint()` request echoCancellation and noiseSuppression applies to every mic, including Dictate and push-to-talk, and has no off switch (MicStream/readme.md says so). Browser noise suppression can clip quiet speech before Whisper, so check Dictate accuracy on the phone.
